newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary K&H Sec downgrades Csopak to 'hold.
newsitem.headline: Hungary K&H Sec downgrades Csopak to 'hold.

text.p: Hungary's K&H Securities said on Monday it had downgraded shares in retailer Csopak to 'hold' from 'buy' following a rally in its price recently.
"One of our favourites, Csopak share price more than doubled in a few days," said K&H Securities's analyst Robert Rethy said in a report.
"That made us downgrade Csopak from 'buy' to 'hold' as the current price seems to reflect its real value."
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Csopak shares hit a life high of 3,295 forints on March 7 and closed at 3,100 forints last Friday.

Nevertheless, K&H Securities, a wholly-owned unit of Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank (K&H Bank), remained upbeat about the company, but said it needed to see Csopak's track record in becoming an integrated retailer.
"Although the company's prospects for the year are still promising, we are waiting for firm confirmation to justify our hopes about the increasingly integrated retailer," Rethy said.
Csopak is 30 percent owned by the East European Food Fund and the company, which is also involved in cosmetics and milling industries, is trying to focus more on food retail.
